Eight suspects were arrested and the servers used to provide illegal access to the channels shut down.<\/p>\n\n<p>A joint investigation led by the <a class=\"external\" href=\"https:\/\/www.policia.es\/\" target=\"_blank\">Spanish National Police<\/a>, with the support of the <a class=\"external\" href=\"http:\/\/www.gdbop.bg\/bg\/\" target=\"_blank\">Bulgarian authorities<\/a>, Europol and <a class=\"external\" href=\"http:\/\/www.eurojust.europa.eu\/Pages\/home.aspx\" target=\"_blank\">Eurojust<\/a>, has resulted in the dismantling of a criminal network specialised in the illegal distribution of pay-TV channels on a European scale.<\/p>\n\n<p>The network is accused of illicitly distributing pay-TV channels in various European countries through two legally established Internet Service Provider (ISP) companies, located in Spain and Bulgaria, by using Internet Protocol television (IPTV) technology.<\/p>\n\n<p>In a coordinated action, eight suspects were arrested and 12 searches carried out simultaneously in Spain and Bulgaria. Investigators seized the servers used to provide illegal access to the channels, alongside numerous documents.<\/p>\n\n<p><img alt=\"Operation Casper\" height=\"375\" src=\"https:\/\/www.europol.europa.eu\/sites\/default\/files\/images\/editor\/op_casper2_0.jpg\" width=\"1514\" loading=\"lazy\"><\/p>\n\n<p>Europol supported the investigations by providing information exchange, operational coordination and support, and forensic expertise. During the investigations, Europol organised an operational meeting at its headquarters in The Hague, and facilitated information exchange between law enforcement agencies and private-sector partners. On the action day, two experts from Europol\u2019s Intellectual Property Crime Coordinated Coalition (IPC3) and two from Europol\u2019s European Cybercrime Centre (EC3) were deployed to Spain and Bulgaria, equipped with mobile offices to support the actions on the spot. This allowed for real-time intelligence analysis and cross-checks against Europol\u2019s databases, as well as forensic support. <\/p>\n\n<p><br>\nOperation Casper began when a representative from a broadcast rights holder filed a complaint against the owner of an Internet Service Provider (ISP) located in M\u00e1laga (Spain), for illicitly distributing pay-TV channels to thousands of clients in different EU countries. Investigations revealed that the ISP owner, a Danish citizen, was the leader of a criminal network who operated on a European scale. Investigators also unveiled the existence of a second ISP in Silistra (Bulgaria) owned by the network, which was permanently connected to the ISP in Spain and provided coverage to other European countries. Both ISPs were legally established in both countries and performed legal activities while, in parallel, exploiting their capacities to carry out illegal activities.<\/p>\n\n<p>The crime group also used a network of shell companies, which relied technically on the ISPs, and were in charge of distributing the illicit TV signals to the end clients.<\/p>\n\n<p>Operation Casper represents a great example of cross-border cooperation against intellectual property rights infringements.<\/p>\n\n<h3>Intellectual property crime in the EU<\/h3>\n\n<p>Intellectual property crime is a significant problem that hits the EU particularly hard. Eight suspects were arrested and the servers used to provide illegal access to the channels shut down.<\/p>\n\n<p>A joint investigation led by the <a class=\"external\" href=\"https:\/\/www.policia.es\/\" target=\"_blank\">Spanish National Police<\/a>, with the support of the <a class=\"external\" href=\"http:\/\/www.gdbop.bg\/bg\/\" target=\"_blank\">Bulgarian authorities<\/a>, Europol and <a class=\"external\" href=\"http:\/\/www.eurojust.europa.eu\/Pages\/home.aspx\" target=\"_blank\">Eurojust<\/a>, has resulted in the dismantling of a criminal network specialised in the illegal distribution of pay-TV channels on a European scale.<\/p>\n\n<p>The network is accused of illicitly distributing pay-TV channels in various European countries through two legally established Internet Service Provider (ISP) companies, located in Spain and Bulgaria, by using Internet Protocol television (IPTV) technology.<\/p>\n\n<p>In a coordinated action, eight suspects were arrested and 12 searches carried out simultaneously in Spain and Bulgaria. Investigators seized the servers used to provide illegal access to the channels, alongside numerous documents.<\/p>\n\n<p><img alt=\"Operation Casper\" height=\"375\" src=\"https:\/\/www.europol.europa.eu\/sites\/default\/files\/images\/editor\/op_casper2_0.jpg\" width=\"1514\" loading=\"lazy\"><\/p>\n\n<p>Europol supported the investigations by providing information exchange, operational coordination and support, and forensic expertise. During the investigations, Europol organised an operational meeting at its headquarters in The Hague, and facilitated information exchange between law enforcement agencies and private-sector partners. On the action day, two experts from Europol\u2019s Intellectual Property Crime Coordinated Coalition (IPC3) and two from Europol\u2019s European Cybercrime Centre (EC3) were deployed to Spain and Bulgaria, equipped with mobile offices to support the actions on the spot. This allowed for real-time intelligence analysis and cross-checks against Europol\u2019s databases, as well as forensic support. <\/p>\n\n<p><br>\nOperation Casper began when a representative from a broadcast rights holder filed a complaint against the owner of an Internet Service Provider (ISP) located in M\u00e1laga (Spain), for illicitly distributing pay-TV channels to thousands of clients in different EU countries. Investigations revealed that the ISP owner, a Danish citizen, was the leader of a criminal network who operated on a European scale. Investigators also unveiled the existence of a second ISP in Silistra (Bulgaria) owned by the network, which was permanently connected to the ISP in Spain and provided coverage to other European countries. Both ISPs were legally established in both countries and performed legal activities while, in parallel, exploiting their capacities to carry out illegal activities.<\/p>\n\n<p>The crime group also used a network of shell companies, which relied technically on the ISPs, and were in charge of distributing the illicit TV signals to the end clients.<\/p>\n\n<p>Operation Casper represents a great example of cross-border cooperation against intellectual property rights infringements.<\/p>\n\n<h3>Intellectual property crime in the EU<\/h3>\n\n<p>Intellectual property crime is a significant problem that hits the EU particularly hard. Eight suspects were arrested and the servers used to provide illegal access to the channels shut down.<\/p>\n\n<p>A joint investigation led by the <a class=\"external\" href=\"https:\/\/www.policia.es\/\" target=\"_blank\">Spanish National Police<\/a>, with the support of the <a class=\"external\" href=\"http:\/\/www.gdbop.bg\/bg\/\" target=\"_blank\">Bulgarian authorities<\/a>, Europol and <a class=\"external\" href=\"http:\/\/www.eurojust.europa.eu\/Pages\/home.aspx\" target=\"_blank\">Eurojust<\/a>, has resulted in the dismantling of a criminal network specialised in the illegal distribution of pay-TV channels on a European scale.<\/p>\n\n<p>The network is accused of illicitly distributing pay-TV channels in various European countries through two legally established Internet Service Provider (ISP) companies, located in Spain and Bulgaria, by using Internet Protocol television (IPTV) technology.<\/p>\n\n<p>In a coordinated action, eight suspects were arrested and 12 searches carried out simultaneously in Spain and Bulgaria. Investigators seized the servers used to provide illegal access to the channels, alongside numerous documents.<\/p>\n\n<p><img alt=\"Operation Casper\" height=\"375\" src=\"https:\/\/www.europol.europa.eu\/sites\/default\/files\/images\/editor\/op_casper2_0.jpg\" width=\"1514\" loading=\"lazy\"><\/p>\n\n<p>Europol supported the investigations by providing information exchange, operational coordination and support, and forensic expertise. During the investigations, Europol organised an operational meeting at its headquarters in The Hague, and facilitated information exchange between law enforcement agencies and private-sector partners. On the action day, two experts from Europol\u2019s Intellectual Property Crime Coordinated Coalition (IPC3) and two from Europol\u2019s European Cybercrime Centre (EC3) were deployed to Spain and Bulgaria, equipped with mobile offices to support the actions on the spot. This allowed for real-time intelligence analysis and cross-checks against Europol\u2019s databases, as well as forensic support. <\/p>\n\n<p><br>\nOperation Casper began when a representative from a broadcast rights holder filed a complaint against the owner of an Internet Service Provider (ISP) located in M\u00e1laga (Spain), for illicitly distributing pay-TV channels to thousands of clients in different EU countries. Investigations revealed that the ISP owner, a Danish citizen, was the leader of a criminal network who operated on a European scale. Investigators also unveiled the existence of a second ISP in Silistra (Bulgaria) owned by the network, which was permanently connected to the ISP in Spain and provided coverage to other European countries. Both ISPs were legally established in both countries and performed legal activities while, in parallel, exploiting their capacities to carry out illegal activities.<\/p>\n\n<p>The crime group also used a network of shell companies, which relied technically on the ISPs, and were in charge of distributing the illicit TV signals to the end clients.<\/p>\n\n<p>Operation Casper represents a great example of cross-border cooperation against intellectual property rights infringements.<\/p>\n\n<h3>Intellectual property crime in the EU<\/h3>\n\n<p>Intellectual property crime is a significant problem that hits the EU particularly hard. quote: Agentes de la Policía Nacional, en una operación conjunta con EUROPOL, han desarticulado una red criminal que presuntamente distribuía contenidos audiovisuales de forma ilegal a más de 500.000 usuarios en varios países europeos. Los cuatro arrestados operaban desde Málaga y se valían de varias páginas web para publicitar paquetes de suscripción compuestos por más de 2.600 canales de televisión y 23.000 películas y series; además, contaban con más de 95 revendedores ubicados en España, Reino Unido, Malta, Portugal, Chipre y Grecia. Los beneficios obtenidos, que ascendían a unos tres millones de euros anuales, eran blanqueados por la organización adquiriendo bienes muebles e inmuebles en la provincia de Málaga y desviando fondos a través de sociedades españolas a cuentas bancarias ubicadas en paraísos fiscales. Durante los registros, los agentes desconectaron 10 paneles de administración -conectados a 32 servidores ubicados en Francia, Países Bajos y España- donde se alojaban los contenidos ilegales de televisión, e intervinieron material informático, 2.800 euros en efectivo y dos vehículos de alta gama valorados en 180.000 euros. La investigación se inició en el año 2020 gracias a una denuncia presentada por los responsables de Alliance for Creativity and Entertainment, una coalición de empresas cuya finalidad es combatir la piratería online. Las primeras gestiones policiales permitieron constatar la existencia de una organización que, desde el año 2012, estaría comercializando y distribuyendo de forma masiva y fraudulenta -a través de distintas sociedades- contenidos audiovisuales de diferentes plataformas televisivas de acceso condicionado a pago. Concretamente, ofertaban a sus clientes diferentes paquetes de suscripción compuestos por más de 2.600 canales de televisión y 23.000 películas y series. Contaban con más de 95 revendedores en diferentes países europeos y blanqueaban beneficios de 3.000.000 de euros anuales Los investigados se valían de varias páginas web para publicitar la promoción y venta de suscripciones de listados ordenados de canales de televisión y descodificadores que, a través de unas claves y contraseñas, permitían visionar los canales y contenidos pertenecientes a diferentes plataformas de televisión de pago. Además, la organización contaba con más de 95 revendedores (resellers) ubicados en Reino Unido, Malta, Portugal, Chipre y Grecia. Estos compraban grandes paquetes de suscripciones de forma piramidal a la organización para posteriormente revenderlos en sus países a miles de usuarios. Por otra parte, los beneficios obtenidos -que ascendían a unos 3.000.000 de euros anuales- los blanqueaban, por un lado, moviendo los fondos procedentes de los pagos de las suscripciones desde sociedades españolas hacia distintas cuentas bancarias a nombre de empresas ubicadas en paraísos fiscales gestionadas por los investigados; y por otro, mediante la compraventa de viviendas y vehículos de lujo o constituyendo nuevas sociedades para amparar la actividad delictiva. Se han desconectado 10 paneles de administración conectados a 32 servidores ubicados en Francia, Países Bajos y España Durante los registros, los agentes accedieron a 10 paneles de administración conectados a 32 servidores ubicados en Francia, Países Bajos y España donde se alojaban los contenidos ilegales de televisión a través de los que la organización ofrecía el servicio. Tras proceder a su desconexión se dejó sin servicio tanto a los revendedores como a los usuarios finales. Asimismo, la investigación ha permitido bloquear ocho cuentas bancarias e intervenir numeroso material informático, documentación, 2.800 euros en efectivo y dos vehículos de alta gama valorados en 180.000 euros. La operación ha finalizado con cuatro detenidos en los municipios malagueños de Benahavís (2), Mijas (una persona detenida y otra investigada) y Benalmádena (1), si bien continúan las gestiones para identificar a más posibles implicados relacionados con la organización en otros países. quote: > Law enforcement agencies from 27 countries* participated in the 13th edition of Operation In Our Sites, a Europol-coordinated operation to take down websites offering counterfeit goods or involved in online piracy. The recurring operation, which is supported by Eurojust and INTERPOL, targets, investigates and seizes websites hosting a variety of illicit content. The main issues continue to be intellectual property infringement on trademarks, as well as on copyrighted content available on internet protocol television (IPTV) and movie streaming services, peer-to-peer sharing platforms and hosting websites. Key findings of the operation that took place from 1 May to 14 November also show that more counterfeit products are being assembled within the European Union's borders and that intellectual property crime is closely intertwined with serious and organised crime.

La acción judicial fue impulsada por LaLiga y la Alianza Contra la Piratería. 24-07-2025 | 15:43 Imagen general con IA En una acción conjunta entre LaLiga de España y la Alianza Contra la Piratería, se concretaron cinco allanamientos simultáneos en Chubut, Mendoza y Río Negro, con el objetivo de desarticular una red de distribución ilegal de contenidos deportivos a través de la plataforma pirata MagisTV . Las órdenes de detención fueron emitidas por el Juzgado de Garantías N.º 4 de San Isidro y ejecutadas con apoyo de la Policía Federal y fuerzas locales. Entre los principales objetivos estuvo el proveedor de internet UV Mundo Digital, con sedes en Trelew y Rawson, que ofrecía dispositivos y suscripciones a MagisTV Pro bajo apariencia de legalidad. La empresa, registrada ante ENACOM y miembro de CABASE, comercializaba los servicios incluso en sus propios locales y redes sociales. Según explicaron desde LaLiga, que actúa como querellante en la causa, este tipo de operaciones refleja “la falta de compromiso” de ciertos proveedores de internet en la lucha contra el fraude audiovisual. “CABASE está influenciada por algunas ISP que no respetan la legalidad”, señaló su presidente de LaLiga, Javier Tebas , quien también destacó el rol de entidades colaboradoras como Mercado Libre y Mercado Pago en la investigación. Tebas (izquierda) durante una acción contra la piratería (Foto: X@LaLiga). Además de los allanamientos, la justicia solicitó la detención de al menos cuatro personas identificadas como operadores clave en la venta ilegal de MagisTV Pro. Estas personas recibían pagos a través de plataformas digitales como Mercado Pago, Naranja X y Binance, y acumularon ingresos que en algunos casos superaron los 160 millones de pesos argentinos . La investigación permitió rastrear evidencias bancarias, registros de IP y comunicaciones extraídas de aplicaciones de mensajería que vinculan directamente a los detenidos con la distribución ilegal de contenidos audiovisuales. El operativo formó parte de una estrategia regional más amplia que tiene como objetivo desarticular redes piratas de IPTV en América Latina . El uso de plataformas ilegales representa también un riesgo para los usuarios, debido a la exposición a malware, estafas digitales y robo de datos personales.  Entre los avances recientes en la lucha antipiratería destacan el desarrollo de bloqueos dinámicos por DNS e IP, la eliminación judicial de aplicaciones como MagisTV y FlujoTV -pendiente aún de ejecución por parte de Google- y la organización del primer “War Room” antipiratería en Argentina.
